title: Why Do Male Seahorses Get Pregnant?
description:
Why do male seahorses get pregnant? The female drops her eggs into a brood pouch on the male's belly, where he supplies oxygen and nutrients through placenta-like blood vessels for about two to four weeks before giving birth to up to a thousand babies, which frees her to make the next batch of eggs sooner.

topic: Why do male seahorses get pregnant?
script: Male seahorses get pregnant, and you've never seen a weirder birth: up to a thousand babies at once. So why him, and not her? After a twirly mating dance, the female drops her eggs into a pouch on the male's belly. He seals them inside and grows tiny blood vessels around them, a lot like a placenta. He feeds them oxygen and nutrients and keeps the water just salty enough. About two to four weeks later, he goes into labor, pumping and squeezing until the babies shoot out in a cloud. Here's the clever bit. While he's busy carrying, she's already making her next batch of eggs. Some dads give birth in the morning and are pregnant again by evening. More babies, way faster. So would you trade jobs with a seahorse dad?
key_facts: The female deposits her eggs into a brood pouch on the male's belly
The male grows blood vessels in the pouch (placenta-like) and supplies oxygen and nutrients, and regulates the pouch's salinity
Pregnancy lasts roughly 10-30 days depending on species (about two to four weeks)
Up to about 1,000 babies per birth (some species up to 2,000)
Leading explanation: the female can produce her next batch of eggs while he is pregnant, shortening the reproductive cycle
Some males can give birth in the morning and be pregnant again by evening
